description: Safe rendering of Markdown and HTML that an LLM, agent or tool produced: sanitizes into a DocumentFragment with DOMPurify, never through innerHTML, and applies a policy for image hosts, link schemes and exfiltration sinks. Streaming aware and Trusted Types compatible. Framework-free core with Angular, React, Mermaid and A2UI packages, an ESLint plugin for HTML sinks, and mcp-app-lint for MCP App security metadata.
rules: Install `@render-policy/core`, plus `@render-policy/angular` or `@render-policy/react` for those frameworks. The packages are ESM only; Node 20.19 and later can `require()` them.

Never show agent output through `innerHTML`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `[innerHTML]` or `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`: use `renderer.renderMarkdownInto(element, text)`, `<RpMarkdown>`, `[rpRender]` or `<rp-markdown>`.

For a streaming reply, use `renderer.createStream(element)`, then `push(chunk)` and `end()`; in Angular and React pass the streaming flag (`[rpRenderStreaming]`, `streaming`) instead of re-rendering by hand.
Modes are `strict`, `balanced` (default) and `permissive`. Balanced blocks remote images whose host is not in `policy.images.hosts`: list your image hosts rather than switching to permissive.
Every decision lands in the journal with a stable `code` (`onDecision`), and application hooks that throw never abort a render.
`@render-policy/core/internal` is outside semver; application code imports from `@render-policy/core`.
Enforce the safe path with `eslint-plugin-render-policy` (`configs.recommended`, `configs['angular-templates']`); check an MCP App's `_meta.ui` CSP and permissions with `mcp-app-lint`.
